title: Ankhorage Data Sources
summary: Provides provider-neutral discovery, normalization, validation, and execution building blocks for REST, GraphQL, and OpenAPI data sources.
purpose: Give independently deployable consumers a canonical way to describe and operate API data sources without coupling their application logic to one transport or provider.
responsibilities: Discover and normalize REST, GraphQL, and OpenAPI operations into canonical data-source representations.
Validate manual and discovered API definitions before execution.
Expose headless package and CLI capabilities for inspecting and testing data-source configurations.
boundaries: Does not own application-specific workflows, credentials, persistence, or user interfaces.
Does not replace transport providers or execute unrelated application capabilities.
Does not depend on a particular hosting platform or consuming application.
audience: Application and tooling authors integrating external APIs through portable data-source definitions.
Provider authors and operators validating data-source configurations.
useCases: Import an OpenAPI document and inspect the operations it exposes.
Normalize GraphQL introspection into executable operation descriptors.
Define, validate, and test a manual REST API configuration.

architecture.role: Reusable headless data-source library with explicit discovery, normalization, execution, and CLI delivery boundaries.
invariants: Portable data-source descriptions remain independent of provider credentials and application-specific state.
Consumers use published entrypoints and declared dependencies rather than repository-local source coupling.
Transport-specific parsing remains behind the package's canonical public operations.

limitations: Live discovery and execution require the caller to provide access to the target API.
Only the REST, GraphQL, and OpenAPI shapes explicitly supported by the package are normalized.
